SHRI UTTAM KUMAR REDDY (NALGONDA): Hon. Chairman Sir, firstly, I wish to thank you for giving me an opportunity to speak on the Demands for Grants pertaining to the Ministry of Agriculture. 

It is a matter of great pride for all Indians that, from a scenario soon after Independence when India was dependent on imports for both food grains and milk powder, today we are one of the global leaders in the production of food grains, milk and horticulture products. Domestic production of food grains went up on an exponential growth post Green Revolution. The White Revolution ensured India’s preeminent position in milk production and the Blue Revolution launched in India during the Seventh Five Year Plan rapidly increased the production of fish and marine products. 

Speaking on the Demands for Grants for the Ministry of Agriculture, through you, I would like to ask the Government on certain points. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare was expected to spend Rs. 75,753 crore in 2018-19 as per the Revised Estimates. However, the provisional accounts maintained by the CGA suggests that the Ministry’s expenditure in 2018-19 was Rs. 53,000 crore which is Rs. 22,000 crore less than the Revised Estimates. It is a shortfall of 29 per cent from the Revised Estimates. I would like the Government to let us know as to how a 29 per cent shortfall could have taken place in the Ministry of Agriculture. 

Today, the Indian farmers are facing a serious agricultural crisis and the position is that, every day, nearly 30 farmers are committing suicide in India. Despite 65 to 70 per cent of our population directly or indirectly dependent on agriculture, the present Government’s low priority to agriculture, inadequate support price, inefficient procurement systems and flawed crop insurance mechanism have resulted in the Indian farming community being pushed into an existential crisis. 

It is very sad that we have to discuss the issue of farmers’ suicides. Over the last few years, 11,000, 12,000, 13,000 farmers’ suicides have been taking place every year. This Government, instead of addressing the issue of farmers’ suicides, prevented NCRB from giving data on farmers’ suicides after 2016. The NCRB was merged with the Bureau of Police Research and Development, and after that, from 2017 onwards, there are no authentic figures of farmers’ suicides available. It shows the wisdom of the Government. The NCRB was merged with the Bureau of Police Research and Development, and it was de-merged 10 months later. Since then, NCRB has not been giving any data on this. Through you, I would like to bring to the notice of the Government that the worst sufferers in this scenario are the tenant farmers. In States like Telangana, there are 30 per cent of tenant farmers, and in the rest of the country, there are 15 per cent of tenant farmers. Today, in India, there are 2.1 crore tenant farmers and almost all of them have no access to bank and institutional finance. So, they have to go to the moneylenders. 

The PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi is not applicable to them. Most of them do not go for crop insurance. So, the tenant farmers are going for high cost money lending and also for commercial crops. When the crop fails, there are a large number of suicides. In the combined Andhra Pradesh State, in 2011-12, to give a legal sanctity to the tenant farmers, we had brought in a new law - Andhra Pradesh Land Licensed Cultivators Act – which made the tenant farmers eligible for institutional finance. Through you, we would urge the Central Government to protect crores of tenant farmers. If you have to give them a legal sanctity, you have to bring in a law like that so that the tenant farmers can be eligible for bank and institutional finance. 

The other point is regarding doubling of farmers’ income. The Government, in its Budget of 2016-17, promised that they will double the farmers’ income by 2022. This has been repeatedly spoken by the hon. Prime Minister. Now, three years have passed, and we have reached the mid-point. Has the Government prepared any Report on what is the increase of farmers’ income in India in these three years? To achieve this goal, the incomes of farmers should have grown by 13 per cent every year for a period six years. The Economic Survey of 2018 shows that the incomes have remained flat with almost no growth. The Economic Survey of January 2018 analysed the issue of farmers’ income. They said that “in the last four years, the level of real agricultural GDP and real agricultural revenues has remained constant.” I have quoted the Economic Survey of January 2018. So, the growth rate in agricultural incomes, in the first four years of NDA Government, was almost zero. We request the Government to tell us how they will be able to double the farmers’ incomes in the balance three years. This reflects the real situation being faced by farmers in the country. Without implementing any concrete solution, this Government is talking about doubling farmers’ incomes by 2022.

Regarding Minimum Support Price, the BJP, in 2014, had categorically stated that if they are elected and would come to power, they would implement the Swaminathan Commission formula for MSP – basically, Cost C2 plus 50 per cent margin. Very surprisingly, in 2015, this BJP Government filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court saying that it is not possible to give 50 per cent margin over the cost of production.

In fact, the words they used were: “prescribing an increase of at least 50 per cent on cost may distort the market.” 

Then on 22nd May 2017, the then Agriculture Minister totally denied that they ever made an election promise of implementing Swaminanthan Committee Report. Again, taking a U-turn, in the Budget Speech of 2018-19, the then Finance Minister announced that they will implement Swaminanthan Committee Report and went a step further and said they already implemented it for a majority of rabi crops. But what they actually did was to use a lower definition of cost, so that they do not have to give the high MSP which they promised. In reality, the rise in MSP in kharif in 2018-19 was not even as high in percentage terms as the MSP rise in 2008-09, 10 years back, given by the then UPA Government. In fact, during UPA-2, the average profit margin over cost of production was higher in almost all the crops compared to the so-called high MSPs of last year. But the most important question is this - whatever MSPs were announced, did the farmer get them? 

I would like to ask the Government, through you, everywhere in India, I am quoting the Government’s report, be it paddy in Uttar Pradesh or West Bengal, or red gram in Maharashtra or Karnataka, or groundnut in Rajasthan or Andhra Pradesh, most of these crops are selling below MSP. Once again, the farmers are asking: what did you promise and what are you delivering? I also wish to bring to the notice of the Government, through you, the Commission which decides the agricultural products pricing had come to Hyderabad and had extensive discussions with the Government officials and others. The MSP recommended was a much higher figure than what is finally approved by this Government. I will give you a simple example. The Minister may also be interested to know. I myself was there on Saturday and Sunday in my constituency. The MSP at the present cost of production of cotton is not 50 per cent; it is not even 25 per cent. It must be borne in mind that the largest number of farmers’ suicides happen in cotton and chilly crops. The then Finance Minister in his 2018-19 Budget Speech promised that the Government will make sure that every farmer will be able to sell at MSP or more than that. 

In September, 2018, the Government announced PM-AASHA scheme, whose purpose is to ensure that every one of the 14.50 crore farmers in India is able to get the benefit of MSP. महोदया, समय के अभाव के कारण मैं बहुत विस्तार से विभागों की अनुदान मांगों की कुछ बातें नहीं कह सकता हूं, लेकिन जो मुख्य बातें हैं, उनको जरूर कहूंगा । कृषि और ग्रामीण विकास को समर्पित इस बजट को देखकर मेरे मन में यह विश्वास हो गया है कि विकास की दौड़ में पीछे रह गए हमारे गांव, गरीब और किसान विकास की मुख्य धारा में शामिल होकर रहेंगे । प्रधान मंत्री जी के कुशल नेतृत्व, दूरदर्शिता और नीयत के बल पर हम वर्ष 2022 तक एक श्रेष्ठ भारत और किसान की आय को दोगुना करने में सफल होंगे । 

सभापति महोदया, तमाम आर्थिक प्रगति, तरक्की और चन्द्रमा तक चन्द्रयान ले जाने में सफल होने के बाद भी हमारी पहचान कृषि प्रधान देश की है । हमारी अर्थव्यवस्था का बहुत बड़ा भाग कृषि पर निर्भर है । कृषि भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था की रीढ़ है और अर्थतंत्र की बुनियाद है । किसान ही देश के अन्नदाता हैं, परंतु बुआई, कटाई से लेकर अपनी फसल और सब्जी को बाजार तक पहुंचाने में किसानों को काफी दिक्कतें आती हैं । कुछ ऐसी समस्याएं हैं और कुछ मौसम की मार किसानों को उनकी फसल का पूरा मूल्य नहीं दे पाती है । हम सब लोग जानते हैं कि कृषि मुख्य रूप से लागत, उत्पादन और लाभकारी मूल्य के साथ मौसम पर भी निर्भर करती है । सभापति जी, खेद है कि आजादी के 60 वर्षों तक अन्नदाता के कुशल क्षेम का पूरी तरह से ध्यान नहीं रखा गया । योजनाएं बनीं, चिंता हुई, मैं इससे इंकार नहीं करता हूं, लेकिन वे जमीन पर साकार नहीं हुईं । पहले भी लाभकारी मूल्य निश्चित किए जाते थे, सरकारें घोषणाएं करती थीं, लेकिन क्रय केन्द्र समय से नहीं खुलते थे, क्रय समय से नहीं होता था । किसान अपना घर चलाने के लिए मजबूरी में बिचौलियों के माध्यम से अन्न बेच देता था । वही बिचौलिए क्रय केन्द्रों पर जाकर सरकारी मूल्य पर लेते थे और किसान ठगा जाता था । मैं बधाई देना चाहता हूं कि आज हमारी केन्द्र सरकार ने अपनी नीतियों को जमीन पर उतारकर जहां लाभकारी मूल्य निश्चित किया है, वहीं उत्पादन खलिहान में आने से पहले ही कृषि केन्द्र या क्रय केन्द्र खोले जा रहे हैं । 

क्रय केन्द्रों के माध्यम से खरीद भी हो रही है और लाभकारी मूल्य उनके खातों में पहुंच रहा है । मैं याद दिलाना चाहता हूं कि इस देश में सारी योजनाओं की घोषणा करने के बाद भी हमारे पूर्व प्रधान मंत्री ने पूरे देश के सामने कहा था कि हम जो गरीबों को देना चाहते हैं, किसानों को देना चाहते हैं, उसका 75 प्रतिशत रास्ते में रह जाता है, केवल 15 प्रतिशत पहुंचता है, लेकिन उसका समाधान नहीं कर पाए थे । मैं बधाई देना चाहता हूं कि हमारे प्रधान मंत्री आदरणीय मोदी जी ने वर्ष 2014 में सत्ता संभालते ही जन-धन योजना में खाता खोलकर 33 करोड़ लोग, जो कृषि पर आधारित थे, कृषि मजदूर थे, खेत और खलिहानों में काम करने वाले थे, बड़ी संख्या में उसमें सम्मिलित थे, आज किसान की खरीद हो, चाहे उसको मिलने वाली सब्सिडी हो, चाहे गरीब को मिलने वाली सुविधाएं हों, वे सीधे उनके खाते में जा रही हैं । इसलिए, आज की सरकार अपनी योजनाओं को साकार करने में सफल हुई है । 

महोदया, सरकार ने आज इस बार शपथ लेने के साथ ही 24 घंटों के अंदर हुई बैठक में जो पहला एजेंडा हुआ, उसमें किसान के कल्याण के लिए अभूतपूर्व कदम उठाते हुए उन्हें पेंशन की कवरेज प्रदान की । अंतरिम बजट में इस योजना का शुभारम्भ हुआ । प्रारम्भ में 2 हेक्टेयर खेती करने वालों को किसान प्रधान मंत्री सम्मान निधि योजना के अंतर्गत 6 हजार रुपये देने की बात थी । एक आंकड़े के अनुसार वर्ष 2019 तक सवा तीन करोड़ लाभार्थियों को बैंक खातों में पहली किश्त और पौने तीन करोड़ लोगों को दूसरी किश्त भी बैंक खातों में सीधे मिल चुकी है । मैं बधाई देना चाहता हूं कि हमारे प्रधान मंत्री जी ने पहली ही कैबिनेट बैठक में ये निर्णय लिये कि जिनके पास भी खेत हैं, अब उसकी कोई सीमा नहीं होगी । ऐसे सभी किसानों को 6 हजार रुपये की सम्मान निधि मिलेगी । कुछ लोगों ने इस पर टिप्पणियां कीं, लेकिन जब उसकी विवेचना करेंगे तो पाएंगे कि 6 हजार रुपये किसान की जीवन रेखा हैं । ऐसे किसान जो सीमांत हैं, लघु हैं, डेढ़ एकड़, दो एकड़, ढाई एकड़ जोतने वाले हैं, जब फसल का समय आता था, तो निश्चित रूप से उनको कहीं न कहीं पूंजी के लिए, बीज खरीदने के लिए, खाद खरीदने के लिए, पानी चलाने के लिए किसी न किसी से कर्ज लेना पड़ता था, सूद देना पड़ता था । उत्पादन का लाभ पाने के बाद वह पैसा उसी सूद और कर्ज में चला जाता था, फिर किसान खाली हाथ हो जाता था, लेकिन यह 6 हजार रुपये की पूंजी उनको मोहताज नहीं करेगी कि किसी से कर्ज मांगें । किसान इन रुपयों से बीज खरीदेंगे, खाद खरीदेंगे और छोटे किसानों के लिए यह पूंजी पर्याप्त होगी और उससे जब लाभ होगा तो पूरा का पूरा लाभ उनको होगा और कुछ लोग कहते हैं कि दोगुना लाभ कैसे होगा? इसी में से दोगुना लाभ होगा । पूंजी सरकार की, उत्पादन का लाभ किसान को, उसको लाभ निश्चित होगा । इसी तरह से सरकार ने सहकारिता एवं कृषि कल्याण मंत्रालय की अनुदान मांग, जो कि मांग संख्या-1 है, के अंतर्गत 1 लाख 30 हजार 485 करोड़ रुपये का विशाल बजट आबंटित किया है । यह बजट वर्ष 2018-19 के बजट से 83 हजार 785 करोड़ रुपये ज्यादा है, जिसके लिए मैं माननीय प्रधान मंत्री जी, वित्त मंत्री जी और कृषि मंत्री जी को बधाई देता हूं । 

उसी तरह पीएम किसान निधि के लिए पिछले वर्ष के रिवाइज्ड एस्टिमेट आबंटन, 2018-19 के 20 हजार करोड़ रुपये को इस वर्ष बढ़ाकर 75 हजार करोड़ रुपये कर दिया गया है । यह उल्लेखनीय है । इस योजना के माध्यम से किसान घरेलू जरूरतों से संबंधित खर्च को पूरा करने में सक्षम हो जाएंगे और उन्हें सूदखोरों के चंगुल में आने से भी बचाया जा सकेगा । 

प्रधान मंत्री किसान पेंशन योजना – छोटे और सीमांत किसानों की त्रासदी यह है कि उनके पास बुढ़ापे के लिए बिलकुल भी बचत नहीं हो पाती है । जब तक उनके शरीर में शक्ति है, परिश्रम करते हैं, श्रम करते हैं, मजदूरी करते हैं और पारिश्रमिक पाते हैं । उससे उनकी रोटी चलती है । लेकिन जब 60 वर्ष से ऊपर के हो जाते हैं और शरीर शीर्ण हो जाता है, वे काम करने की स्थिति में नहीं रहते हैं, श्रम नहीं कर सकते हैं तो रोटी के लिए मोहताज हो जाते हैं । ऐसे किसानों के लिए सरकार ने किसान पेंशन योजना लागू की है । साथ ही किसानों को बुढ़ापे में पेंशन दी जाए, इसको सुनिश्चित किया । इस योजना के तहत 60 वर्ष की आयु प्राप्त करने पर पात्र लघु और सीमांत किसानों को तीन हजार रुपये की न्यूनतम पेंशन दी जाएगी । इस स्कीम का टारगेट पहले तीन वर्ष के दौरान पांच करोड़ लाभार्थियों को इसके अंतर्गत लाना है । यह एक स्वैच्छिक और अंशदायी स्कीम है, जिसमें शामिल होने की आयु 18 वर्ष से 40 वर्ष की है । मैं वित्त मंत्री जी का आभार प्रकट करता हूं कि उन्होंने इस स्कीम के लिए वर्ष 2022 तक के लिए 10775 करोड़ रुपये का बजटीय प्रावधान अनुमोदित किया है । साथ ही, मैं उन्हें बधाई भी देना चाहता हूं । वित्त मंत्री जी जब बजट भाषण का जवाब दे रही थीं, तो उन्होंने घोषणा की थी कि यह पेंशन योजना केवल खेती करने वालों के लिए ही नहीं, अपितु कृषि पर आधारित जो मजदूर हैं, जिनकी रोजी कृषि के माध्यम से चलती है, अब उनके लिए भी लागू की जाएगी, इसके लिए उनको बधाई । 

कृषि उत्पाद को बढ़ावा देने के लिए सरकार ने अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण योजना किसान मृदा स्वास्थ्य एवं उर्वरता योजना प्रारम्भ की है । जिससे किसानों को बड़ा लाभ पहुंच रहा है । इस योजना के अंतर्गत सरकार ने वर्ष 2019-20 में 324.20 करोड़ रुपये का आबंटन किया है, जो उल्लेखनीय है । सरकार ने इस कड़ी में एक ऐसी नई योजना शून्य बजट प्राकृतिक कृषि की शुरुआत भी की है, जिसे अपनाकर किसान अपनी फसल का उत्पादन दोगुना कर सकते हैं । 

ई-नाम योजना की भी एक नई शुरुआत की गई है । जिसके अंतर्गत वर्ष 2019-20 में देश भर में चुनिंदा एक हजार मंडियों में कृषि जिंसों के व्यापार के लिए शुरू किए गए ई-नाम सॉफ्टवेयर से जुड़ने के इच्छुक राज्यों और यूनियन टैरिटरीज़ क्षेत्रों में थोक मंडियों के लिए एक सामान्य ई-मंडी प्लेटफार्म की स्थापना का प्रयास किया जा रहा है । 

महोदय, किस-किस विषय पर कहा जाए, इस विस्तार में जाए बगैर मैं कहना चाहता हूं कि वर्ष 2014 से 2019 तक की अवधि में किसानों को सशक्त बनाने के लिए अनगिनत कदम उठाए गए हैं, जैसे 22 फसलों के न्यूनतम समर्थन मूल्य में वृद्धि की गई है । किसानों की लागत में कमी लाना । इसी देश का किसान यूरिया खरीदने के लिए लाइन में खड़ा होता था । लाठियां भी बरसती थीं और फिर भी ब्लैक मार्किट में यूरिया महंगे दामों पर लेनी पड़ती थी । लेकिन हमारे प्रधान मंत्री की नीतियों से नीम कोटेड यूरिया का प्रयोग किया गया । अब यूरिया की कोई कमी नहीं है । आज यूरिया सरल सुलभ है, सस्ता है, समय से मिल रहा है, बिना लाइन के मिल रहा है । इससे किसान खुशहाल है ।

‘प्रधान मंत्री कृषि सिंचाई योजना’ और ‘प्रधान मंत्री किसान संपदा योजना’ से किसानों को जमीनी स्तर पर बहुत लाभ पहुंचा है । कृषि अनुसंधान और कृषि शिक्षा पर भी सरकार ने पूरा ध्यान दिया है । डिमांड फॉर ग्रान्ट्स के अंतर्गत मांग संख्या दो में कृषि अनुसंधान एवं शिक्षा विभाग के अंतर्गत बजट दिया गया है । बजट को वर्ष 2018 में 7,800 करोड़ रुपयों से बढ़ाकर 8,078.76 करोड़ रुपये किया गया है, जो कि कृषि अनुसंधान के लिए 278 करोड़ रुपये की ज्यादा मदद है । इसके अंतर्गत पूर्वोत्तर क्षेत्रों पर विशेष ध्यान देते हुए 486 करोड़ रुपयों का ज्यादा आबंटन किया गया है । इसमें पशु पालन, दुग्ध और मत्स्य पालन पर जोर दिया गया है ।

महोदया, पहली बार इस सरकार ने शिद्दत से यह महसूस किया है कि केवल खेती से किसान की आय नहीं बढ़ पाएगी । पहले भी जब परंपरागत खेती थी, तब भी किसानों की अतिरिक्त आय के लिए पशुपालन ही उनका सबसे बड़ा आधार था । इसके लिए पशुपालन, दुग्ध और मत्स्य पालन मंत्रालय का गठन किया गया है, जिसके लिए मैं प्रधान मंत्री जी को बधाई देना चाहता हूं, जो यह दर्शाता है कि यह सरकार किसानों की आय बढ़ाने के लिए कृतसंकल्प है । वर्ष 2019-20 के बजट में वित्त मंत्री जी ने डेयरी और पशुधन के लिए मांग संख्या 40 के अंतर्गत 2,932.25 करोड़ रुपयों का विशाल बजट दिया है, जिसका मैं स्वागत करता हूं । 

महोदया, यही नहीं, इन कृषि सहायक क्षेत्रों में सरकार ने इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर बढ़ाने के लिए प्रयास किए हैं, जैसे राष्ट्रीय गोकुल मिशन । इसके अंतर्गत सरकार ने अच्छी किस्में, देशी नस्लों का विकास और वैज्ञानिक तरीके से संकर किस्में बनाने पर जोर दिया है । इस सरकार ने आते ही पशुधन सुरक्षा से संबंधित एक महत्वपूर्ण फैसला लेते हुए पशुओं के टीकाकरण का बीड़ा भी अपने कंधों पर उठाया है । इसमें खुरपका और मुंहपका जैसी अन्य बीमारियों को पूरी तरह से नियंत्रित करने के लिए प्रयास करना है । वर्ष 2030 तक इन बीमारियों का उन्मूलन करना है । इस योजना के लिए वित्त मंत्री जी ने 500 करोड़ रुपये का बजट इस वर्ष दिया है, जिसका मैं स्वागत करता हूं । मेरा पूरा विश्वास है कि इस टीकाकरण से न केवल घरेलू उत्पादन में वृद्धि होगी, बल्कि दूध और पशुधन के उत्पादन में भी बढ़ोतरी होगी । जब पशु स्वस्थ होंगे, तो निश्चित ही दूध भी बढ़ेगा । 

इसी तरह से मछली पालन को प्रोत्साहन देने के लिए इस सरकार ने अलग से एक मत्स्य पालन विभाग का सृजन किया है । इस विभाग को मांग संख्या 39 के तहत वर्ष 2019-20 के बजट में कुल 804.75 करोड़ रुपये का आबंटन किया गया है, जिसका मैं स्वागत करता हूं । प्रधान मंत्री जी ने देश में मछली उत्पादन और निर्यात को बढ़ाने के लिए नीली क्रांति का आह्वान किया है । उस क्रांति को गति देने के लिए इस बजट में केन्द्र सरकार द्वारा मत्सिकी एकीकृत विकास एवं प्रबंधन के लिए एक नई योजना बनाई गई है । मत्स्य पालन और जलीय कृषि के विकास की इस नवीन योजना को 550 करोड़ रुपये का आबंटन किया गया है । मछुआरों और तटीय जल कृषि जैसे सिंघाड़ा, मखाना इत्यादि के उत्पादन की दृष्टि से विशेष योजनाएं बनाई गई हैं, जिसके अंतर्गत 10 करोड़ रुपये की मत्स्य पालन और जलीय कृषि इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर विकास निधि स्थापित की गई है । यह प्रशंसनीय है । कृषि और गांव को अलग नहीं किया जा सकता है । 

महोदया, कृषि का विकास बिना गांव के विकास के संभव नहीं है और गांव का जो मूलभूत स्वरूप है, उसका विकास बिना कृषि के संभव नहीं है । ग्रामीण विकास पर हमारी सरकार सन् 2014 से ही कार्य कर रही है । गांव के विकास को ही धुरी बना कर बाकी सारी ग्रामीण योजनाएं तैयार की गई हैं । इस बजट में ग्रामीण विकास को गति देते हुए सरकार ने सन् 2018-19 के सापेक्ष जो 1,12,400 करोड़ रुपये के आबंटन को बढ़ा कर 1,17,647.19 करोड़ रुपये कर दिया है । मांग संख्या 84 में यह वृद्धि 5,242 करोड़ रुपये की अभूतपूर्व बढ़ोतरी है, जिसका मैं स्वागत करता हॅूं ।

महोदया, इसी क्रम में मैं मनरेगा की चर्चा करना चाहता हॅूं । मनरेगा के आबंटन के 55 हजार करोड़ रुपये से बढ़ा कर 60 हज़ार करोड़ रुपये कर दिया गया है । कस्बों में विकास के लिए एक विशिष्ट योजना – डॉ. श्यामा प्रसाद मुखर्जी अर्बन मिशन के लिए 800 करोड़ रुपये दिए गए हैं । मैं इस कदम का स्वागत करता हॅूं । इसके अंतर्गत ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में समेकित परियोजनाओं के आधार पर अवसंरचना का उपलब्ध कराना, आर्थिक कार्यकलापों, कौशल विकास करना, मिशन के अंतर्गत ग्रामीण जीवन के मूल स्वरूप को बनाए रखते हुए गांवों को क्लस्टर अर्बन गांवों के रूप में विकसित करना है । इसी तरह से दीन दयाल उपाध्याय ग्रामीण कौशल योजना के तहत ग्रामीण युवाओं के लिए रोजगार जुटाने के लिए प्रयास किए जाते हैं । ग्रामीण बुनियादों का ढांचा बनाने के लिए बजट में प्रधान मंत्री ग्राम सड़क योजना के लिए तीसरे चरण घोषणा की गई है । इसके तहत पांच वर्षों में 1.25 लाख किलोमीटर लंबी सड़कों का निर्माण करने की योजना है, जिसका कुल बजट 80,250 करोड़ रुपये निर्धारित किया गया है । वित्त मंत्री जी ने प्रधान मंत्री ग्राम सड़क योजना सन् 2019-20 19 हजार करोड़ रुपये आबंटित किए हैं । इसी तरह ग्रामीण आवास निर्माण के दूसरे चरण में सन् 2019-20 से 2021-22 के बीच लगभग 1.95 करोड़ नए घर बनाए जाने की योजना है । महत्वपूर्ण बात यह है ÉÊBÉE पहले चरण में 82 हजार करोड़ रुपये की लागत से एक करोड़ घर बनाए गए हैं । 

महोदया, इस वर्ष के आर्थिक सर्वेक्षण के आंकड़ों से एक बात निकल कर आई है । …(व्यवधान)

माननीय सभापति : आपका समय समाप्त हो गया है । अब आप खत्म करें ।

…(व्यवधान)

श्री रमापति राम त्रिपाठी: महोदया, बस पांच मिनट और । …(व्यवधान)

माननीय सभापति: पांच मिनट नहीं, अब आप खत्म करें ।

…(व्यवधान)

श्री रमापति राम त्रिपाठी: महोदया, मैं पहली बार बोल रहा हॅूं । पिछले साल जुलाई से शहरी क्षेत्रों की तुलना में ग्रामीण इलाकों में मंहगाई की दर कम रही है, जो कि इस बात का प्रत्यक्ष प्रमाण है ÉÊBÉE मोदी सरकार की जनहितकारी, विकासकारी और कल्याणकारी योजनाओं का प्रभाव ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में दिखने लगा है ।

महोदया, मैं आपकी अनुमति से कुछ अपनी क्षेत्रीय समस्यों का उल्लेख करना चाहूंगा । मैं उत्तर प्रदेश के देवरिया से चुन कर आता हॅूं । मेरा क्षेत्र कृषि प्रधान इलाका है । कृषि पर आधारित मजदूरों का इलाका है । वहां पर जो स्थिति है, वैसे लगभग 12 जिले इधर और सटा हुआ बिहार है,उसके भी सात-आठ जिलों को मिला कर कृषि अनुसंधान, कृषि शिक्षा, तकनीकी जानकारी के लिए कोई केंद्र नहीं है । मैं बताना चाहता हॅूं कि सन् 1954 में देवरिया जिले में बाबा राघव दास, जो प्रसिद्ध स्वतंत्रता संग्राम सेनानी थे, उनके नाम पर एक कृषि स्नातकोत्तर विद्यालय चल रहा है, जो अपने संसाधनों से लगभग 12 संकायों के द्वारा शोध कर रहा है और लेागों को शिक्षित कर रहा है । 

जो अपने संसाधनों से लगभग 12 संकायों के द्वारा शोध कर रहा है, लोगों को शिक्षित कर रहा है । मैं आपके माध्यम से माननीय कृषि मंत्री जी से आग्रह करूँगा कि उस क्षेत्र की स्थिति को ध्यान में रखते हुए, चूँकि कृषि का विकास करना है, आय को दुगुना करना है, जो प्रधान मंत्री जी की महत्वाकांक्षी योजना है, तो निश्चित ही उसको वैज्ञानिक आधार भी देना होगा, शोध भी बढ़ाना होगा, तकनीकी शिक्षा भी देनी होगी । इसलिए बाबा राघवदास स्नाकनोत्तर महाविद्यालय को विश्वविद्यालय का दर्जा दिया जाए, विश्वविद्यालय में परिवर्तित किया जाए । यह मेरी माँग है ।

दूसरी चीज, मैं उल्लेख करना चाहता हूँ कि प्रधान मंत्री किसान बीमा योजना में यह स्थिति आई है कि हमारे पूर्वी जिलों, जिनमें गोरखपुर, महाराजगंज, सिद्धार्थ नगर, देवरिया और कुशीनगर हैं, अचानक अतिवृष्टि हुई । खेत पानी से लबालब भर गए, मकान गिर गए और उल्लेखनीय बात है कि रोपाई के समय जिन लोगों ने बेहन डाली थी, बेहन अभी जमी थी, वह डूब गई । जिन लोगों ने थोड़ी पहले रोपाई कर दी थी, वह खेत भी डूब गए और नष्ट हो गए । किसान इससे त्रस्त हो गया । जहाँ बरसात से खुशी हुई, वही जो लोग इसमें कुछ आगे बढ़ गए थे, उनकी स्थिति दयनीय हो गई, इसलिए इस स्थिति को भी बीमा में कवर किया जाए । यह मेरी माँग है । साथ ही, मुझे आशा ही नहीं पूरा विश्वास है कि इन प्रयासों से भारतीय कृषि, पशुपालन, ग्रामीण विकास को एक नई गति मिलेगी ।

अंत में, कृषि, ग्रामीण विकास की अनुदान माँगों 1, 2, 3, 9, 30 और 84 के समर्थन में मैं अपनी बात कहते हुए, आपने समय दिया, आप सब लोगों ने सुना, इसके लिए धन्यवाद देते हुए अपनी बात समाप्त करता हूँ । धन्यवाद ।

“UzhudhuNdu Vaazhvaarae Vaazhvaar

The meaning is that the farmers who plough the field are the ones who truly live and rest others are subservient eating what the farmers produce. You say that you have plans to provide Rs.6000 per annum as financial support to each and every farmer of this country. Finance Minister said with pride that this is the only Union Government which has fixed the MSP of all the products. pricing of agricultural products since the year 1985-86. We accept that growth in agriculture has not been up to the mark. In this scenario, how can the people of this country believe that the Government will double the income of farmers. If you compare the Budget Estimate provided for the Ministry of Agriculture in the present Budget with the previous year, there is no considerable increase in the allocation if we kept aside the funds earmarked for implementation of financial support scheme of Rs. 6,000 per annum to farmers. This is the ground reality, I want to ask this Government that how can you reach your targets?. If the farmers’ income is dependant only on agriculture, the farmer, from birth to death, has to live debt-ridden.

If you see the related sectors, India occupies a prominent place in milk production. Approximately 20 per cent of the milk produced throughout the world is from India. Even after record production of milk in this country and even after fixing import duty on milk products at 40 per cent, why the imports have not come down? There is no clear vision on the part of Government to reduce the import of milk products in the country. You have to give importance to research and development activities. Another important sector is poultry. Even after imposing 30 percent of import duty on poultry products, how KFC and other MNCs are establishing their base in different States of our country? We are good at cooking as well as eating.

Our poultry research organization should compete with other MNCs in this field, Our poultry farmers have selling of eggs as their only source of income. price for eggs. Import of chicken legs should be banned. I want to bring to your notice that our hens do have legs. In fisheries sector, we are the third largest producer of fish in the world.

In the fish production, we are the third largest in the world. Approximately 65 per cent is domestic production. By way of exports we earned approximately Rs.45,000 Crore during the previous years. I wish to state that only then, the farmers can get remunerative price for their produce. There should be increase in farm loans on one side. I am happy to say that several agricultural schemes have been implemented by this Government. But there is big gap between the statistics provided by this Government and the ground reality. The new farm loan policy was introduced during the year 2004-05. That time the amount of disbursal by the Nationalized banks, private banks and cooperative banks was fixed at Rs.80000 Crore. This amount was made threefold in three years to reach Rs. 2,40,000 Crore. Due to this effect now the farm loan disbursal has reached Rs. 13 lakh Crore. in industrial sector along with the loans if you waive for farming sector every year.

SHRIMATI PRATIMA MONDAL (JAYNAGAR): Madam Chairperson, I rise to speak on the Demands for Grants under the Ministries of Rural Development, and Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare for 2019-20. 

16.01 hrs (Shri Rajendra Agrawal in the Chair) 

Before coming to the subject, I would like to draw the attention of the House to an important thing. The Union Government has so proudly announced that Indian economy will reach USD 3 trillion by the end of financial year 2020 and thereby overtake the UK economy. Before the Government uses this as another banner for inflating its ever-growing balloon of public brain-washing propaganda, I would like to posit a fact which this Government has continuously overlooked. 

In 2018, India overtook France as the sixth largest economy in the world at USD 2.6 trillion. But what this Government does not tell its people is that France being country of a mere 65 million people was generating a GDP of USD 2.58 trillion while India - the home of a continent size population of 1.3 billion - is housed by a USD 2.6 trillion economy. And soon this figure will surpass that of UK, a country with 66 million people. And again, when India inevitably passes this mere feat of overtaking another European country with a smaller set of people, the real picture will never be brought to light and the headlines will keep fooling the common man. 

So, what is it that really matters to the common man of our country? While the headlines of being a part of the fifth largest economy in the world will give him a hollow sense of pride, at the end of the day, he will ask, “what is my benefit in this; what is my purchasing power; and why has it not gone up to the desired level?”

I now come to sector-specific problems and to the interests of the common man. It is accurate to say that ‘Bharat gaon mein basta hai’ – India lives in its villages. This is so because rural India comprises of 67 per cent of the total Indian population. This majority population lags far behind the urban standard in all terms. While we are all aware that when even urban areas are not in a healthy position, we can imagine how bad the condition of Gramin Bharat would be.

The economy of this region is majorly dependent on agriculture which contributes a meagre 15.87 per cent to the GDP. With the vision of five trillion economy, how much does the Government seek to put into the hands of the majority? Or will it carry on the similar ongoing propaganda where 73 per cent of the wealth is concentrated in the hands of one per cent of the population?

Farmers’ income witnessed a record 14-year low in October to December 2018. The gross value added being a low single digit reflects the reality.

In the election mandate of the ruling party, agriculture held the most important platform. This sector could have found its benefit in this Budget but it has failed to do so. I would like to elaborate so that common man knows what is the reality because simply allotment of fund does not ensure development.

Firstly, Sir, the allocation for the Ministry of Rural Development has fallen from 4.7 per cent in 2018-19 to 4.4 per cent in 2019-20 in terms of its share in the total Budget. Thus, the shout out that it has been allotted Rs. 5,200 crore more than the last year is absolutely baseless. It has rather decreased in terms of share and 0.3 per cent is a huge value.

Sir, the Government pats its back for achieving a great deal in electrifying India. The Finance Minister also mentioned in her Budget that all the homes that are willing will be electrified fully. So, my question is this. Did the Government try to identify the reason behind this aversion to technology or spin this thread into a cloth displaying its own false success? It is very sad to note that 31 million houses are still in dark because 10 per cent of household of a village having a mere bulb is considered electrified according to the Government. Again, Sir, the reality of Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana Scheme is not as bright as depicted because it is not the brain child of this Government. It subsumed already running Rajiv Gandhi Gramin LPG Vitaran Yojana. Even, more importantly, to boost its success rate, the Government added existing BPL subscriber number of almost 1.7 crore people just to create a hype. The Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell confirms anomalies in reporting system as well. It is also necessary to note that 13 per cent or 3.25 crore LPG consumers are inactive – highest in Haryana, a massive 40 per cent. It seems that the Government is playing with the people’s mind by showcasing a set of numbers. I would like to put forth a report of CAG which mentioned that:

“Before Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana Scheme was launched, households with LPG connections were using an average of 6.27 cylinders in a year but that came down to 5.6 cylinders after the launch of the scheme.”

So, what is your excuse for this, hon. Prime Minister ji? The data is absolutely authentic.

Now, coming to the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, it is terrifying to note that there exists no block or district level reporting on the Scheme. Only State level data is available. The CAG report states that:

“In many States like Gujarat and Jharkhand, in violation of the rules, completion of houses was taking more than two years.”

Till December 2018, only 8 per cent of the target was achieved and by half of 2019, 1.54 crore houses are claimed to be completed. This is just misleading people. ‘Housing for All by 2022’ is an absolute political gimmick. It is a great initiative that Jal Shakti Mantralaya has been constituted. But what about the failure of numerous water supply schemes like Swajal Yojana.

Sir, if that would have been a success, more than half of India would have not been suffering due to unfortunate drought condition. Even, international bodies and media are questioning the capabilities of India in the matter of Chennai water scarcity. When will the Government really work and not just keep praising itself, while in reality, masses are suffering?

Secondly, in agriculture we were expecting structural changes which amounted to be nil in this Budget. Instead, the Government is following the ‘carrot and stick’ policy of the Britishers. On one hand, the Government is awarding a sum of Rs. 6000 per annum to farmers. On the other hand, it is pushing them to follow the same old infrastructure which needs a change. There are multiple dimensions to agrarian distress. The first one is high input cost; second is limited access of institutional finance to the marginalised farmers; third is the exploitative nature in which only one-third of the retail prices reaches the farmers; and fourth is that the PDS system does not undertake procurement operation for 24 crops for which the Minimum Support Price is announced.

The Government’s claims of successful schemes like Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana and eNAM are not reflected in reality. How long will it take us to understand that loan waiving and economic support is not the key to resolve the problems of this sector? Had it been so, we would have witnessed a decrease in suicides of farmers. In Maharashtra alone, the suicide toll has risen by 91 per cent in the last four years. We are facing severe drought conditions all across India in 2019. In this scenario, the number of people seeking jobs under MGNREGA is bound to go up. But what did the Government do? It reduced the allotment by Rs. 1084 crore. How fair is that? The Minister even identified 1592 critical blocks but did not indicate any proposal to address this challenge. 

The Finance Minister talked about the Zero Budget Farming. Going back to the basics, how is it possible when there is almost no extended help in the field of fertilizers? During the last five years, subsidy in urea was not touched upon and this was repeated yet again. Without any reform in fertilizer subsidy scheme, it is unrealistic to expect the farmers to switch to organic farming. Here it is very important to note that widespread use of glyphosate is harming the nation as it is a proven carcinogenic element and has been banned in numerous countries while we are serving it on the plates. 

I would like to take this opportunity to throw some light on the successful schemes in my State. Under the hon. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee’s Government, there is one Jal Dharo, Jal Bharo scheme which aims at citizen’s awareness for rainwater conservation and effective water use in irrigation. This has yielded positive results. Today, in Bengal there exists no house which is deprived of water. In Bengal, farmers’ income has increased three times in the past seven years due to several innovative schemes taken up by the hon. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. The Krishak Bandhu scheme supports the cause of farmers and landless labourers in the State. I would like to conclude by putting forth a metaphor which will explain the current situation in India. 

Let us consider the Government to be a surgeon and the Indian economy to be its patient and the Indian population as the family members of the patient. What this surgeon is doing is that he is not giving the patient its requirement. Instead, he is giving the patient a make-up on the outside while the primary organs inside are deteriorating and also fooling its family by showing the exterior which does not show the real picture, telling them all is well and good, before it is too late for them to save the situation. 

Thank you, hon. Chairperson, Sir, for giving me this opportunity and I hope the hon. Minister will clarify my observations as I have put forth here.

SHRI POCHA BRAHMANANDA REDDY(NANDYAL): Hon. Chairman, Sir, at the outset, I would like to thank you for giving me an opportunity to speak at the altar of democracy, where many great people have strived hard to transform the lives of people. Being a first time Member, this is my maiden speech in the House. I wish to learn and contribute to the proceedings of the House in the days to come.

I hail from Nandyal constituency of Andhra Pradesh, where India’s first freedom fighter Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy and great philanthropist Budda Vengal Reddy were born. I feel happy and proud to inform this august House that I represent a constituency which the former President of India, Dr. Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy garu and the former Prime Minister of India, Shri P.V. Narasimha Rao had represented. 

I must bring to the notice of the Government the serious crisis being faced by the rural India, mainly agricultural sector. The Government has taken a few measures to solve the agrarian crisis and double the farmers’ income by 2022. I may mention here some of the steps taken by the Government to solve the agrarian crisis. They are:

1. Transferring Rs.6,000 per year directly into the accounts of small and marginal farmers.

2. Set up eNAMs and eGrams

3. Introduced Soil Health Cards

4. Guaranteed one-and-a-half times of MSP for the farmers

5. Revamping 99 big canal irrigation projects under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana.

Due to the collective result of all the above measures and many others, there has been a record production of cereals, vegetables, fruits, milk and fish.

Rural India is suffering from chronic economic distress, high rate of unemployment, and farmers’ suicide continue to rise. In many of the rural areas, no one is willing to marry farmers, thereby creating huge social distress along with economic distress. Agriculture growth had been slow and has been accompanied by serious dip in wage growth. Rural wages grew at an estimated 3.8 per cent year on year in December 2018. Due to inflation, it drops down to a paltry 2.3 per cent, the lowest ever in the past 15 years. This has led to widespread protests across the country.

Minimum Support Price was increased by one-and-a-half times in 2017 Budget, however, the method of calculating the MSP has flawed. It does not count the rent of land and management cost, which means the measure could not provide full remunerative prices to the farmers. However, in the past, MSP was available for only wheat and paddy. Under the PM-AASHA Scheme, MSP has been fixed for 23 commodities like pulses, oilseeds, millets, cotton, and jute. In the last four years, the Government has transferred Rs.75,000 crore to the farmers by procuring these 23 commodities, minus wheat and paddy, and to that extent, it has worked.

The Government wanted to provide water to every field. It has introduced the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayi Yojana and has proposed to allocate Rs.50,000 crore. However, in the last five years, actual allocation made was only Rs.9,050 crore.

While the reforms are generally considered good and a welcome step, most of the time, they have failed to achieve the objectives because they did not connect the last mile of tenant farmers and farm labourers. They form an important backbone of agriculture in India due to skewed ownership of land because of the historical reasons. Some of the reforms of this Government have, no doubt, helped the agriculture sector, but India is a unique country and it requires unique solutions. One-size-fits-all approach of the Western world will not work for India. If really farmers’ income is doubled, their children will not have to look for jobs outside and thus migration will be reduced.

I hail from Rayalaseema, which is a drought prone and rain shadow area with insufficient water resources.

I am an agriculturalist by education and profession and I have a first-hand experience of rural and countryside areas in India. In Rayalaseema, young people are migrating to other States as there is a huge shortage of drinking water and irrigation water. There are many irrigation canals built over a period of time which require modernisation. I would request the Government to allocate PMKSY funds to modernise canal and construct Siddeswaram weir to provide water facility so that the distressed migration and crisis can be reduced.

KC Canal is one of the oldest canals in India and is providing irrigation and drinking water facilities to a part of Rayalaseema. Of late, the canal is not getting adequate water. I request the Government to sanction funds under PMKSY to build a reservoir at Gundrevula in Kurnool district with a capacity of 20 tmc on Tungabhadra River. It will help ease some problems. Hon. Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, Shri Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy Garu and hon. Chief Minister of Telangana, Shri K. Chandrashekar Rao Garu have embarked on a gigantic activity of linking Godavari river to Krishna river so that the scarcity of water in Krishna River can be bridged with surplus water of Godavari. I request the Central Government to actively support both the Governments and share the cost of such a great humanitarian activity which will solve the water problem in both the States for a very long time to come and benefit upper riparian States like Karnataka and Maharashtra too.

Our beloved former hon. Chief Minister, late Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy, fondly called YSR by people, had embarked on the journey of Jalayagnam and took up huge projects like Polavaram, Handri-Neeva lift irrigation, Galeru Nagari lift irrigation, Pothireddypadu head regulator and many more to provide water to the parched regions of Rayalaseema. All those projects are at various stages of completion. I request the Central Government to provide additional grants to those projects. 

Hon. Chairperson, Sir, the Centre has constituted Krishna River Management Board to manage the allocation of water. I request the Central Government to locate their office in Kurnool.

Hon. Chairperson, Sir, my constituency, Nandyal, is one of the biggest seed production centres in India. I am a Post Graduate in Agriculture and being a farmer, I am running my own seed farm successfully and am helping small and marginalised farmers in my own way. I have built private storage godowns facility as a part of Grameen Bhandar Yojana. I am happy to inform you that it was implemented nationwide after a team has covered it in their documentary. 

Rayalaseema is blessed with all diverse kinds of soils and crops and with the help of Centre, we can do wonders in seed production. My teacher and a great international scientist, Shri Ravindra Nath Garu developed a new cotton seed called ‘Narasimha’, named after our former hon. Prime Minister late Shri P.V. Narasimha Rao Garu. ‘Narasimha’ has become most famous and sought-after seed in India, in no time. The famous Kurnool Sona Masoori Rice is from our region. 

Hon. Chairperson, Sir, there are nearly 1000 acres of land available in my constituency. We want an agriculture college and a research centre. 

Finally, before thanking you for giving me this opportunity, I would suggest immediate, short and long-term measures to ease the agricultural crisis: Establish agriculture universities as many as possible and development of short-term diploma courses like seed production, pest control, soil testing, apiculture, sericulture, etc., along with regular under-graduate courses; provide monetary and economic support to students willing to study agriculture as a subject and encourage them with investments; on-time credit facility to farmers; strict control of middlemen and horse-play games of the traders; provide free transportation facility to farming community; highly effective and pragmatic Minimum Support Price for the major crops; provide support to agro-based industry so that agriculture can be connected to industry; quick completion of ongoing irrigation projects and build as many irrigation projects as possible at the same time with effective water management techniques; and build post-harvest godowns to store the agriculture produce safely. Israel has done very well in water management. We have a huge space industry and the Government should consider commissioning agriculture specific satellite to help pest monitoring, NPK monitoring and yield monitoring and forecasting.

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Please conclude.

SHRI POCHA BRAHMANANDA REDDY : Hon. Chairperson, Sir, thank you once again. I would like to thank the people of my constituency and our hon. Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh for giving me the opportunity.
